beats.text: November twenty-fourth. A small plane carrying six people falls out of the sky, and into the Gulf of Mexico.
The aircraft: a single-engine Cessna two-ten. On board, a family from Florida, heading home after a fishing trip in Louisiana.
It took off from New Orleans Lakefront Airport, bound for Fort Myers, Florida.
But over the Mississippi Sound, near Horn Island, something went terribly wrong.
According to the F.A.A., the plane was descending at about ten thousand feet per minute. Far faster than any normal descent.
Around three forty-five P.M., controllers in Mobile alerted the Coast Guard. Contact was lost.
Rescuers found three life jackets, a life raft, and the plane's cabin, floating on the water.
About four hours later, state divers found all six inside the fuselage. Among them, children.
The Coast Guard called it a heartbreaking outcome. The N.T.S.B. is now leading the investigation.
The question investigators must answer: what made this plane fall so fast?
